# Unwrapped cell drawings and AutoFit

Original fixture generated by `tools/cell_anchor_autofit_fixture.py` from our
original mixed-cell-anchors control. No corpus artwork or source is included.
The generator uses lxml (BSD) and standard-library ZIP/XML operations.

Nine pages combine picture widths 36/72/90 pt with horizontal offsets -6/0/6 pt.
Each page has a two-column AutoFit table with 72 pt preferred cell widths,
6 pt horizontal margins, and a column/paragraph-relative wrapNone picture.
The reference application exported the committed PDF. PDFium renders at 96 DPI;
reference.json records PDF cell-fill bounds and picture frames in points
from the page's top-left. hashes.json identifies the native evidence.

The reference application retains both 72 pt columns in all cases, including pictures overflowing
the right edge. The previous engine enlarged the picture column and sometimes
wrapped neighboring text. All nine native/browser content pairs were inspected.
Unit coverage checks widths and picture positions against the native reference,
then resizes a picture and checks geometry/export/reopen/undo. Browser coverage
compares picture masks bidirectionally within one pixel and checks text editing,
package preservation, undo, and reopening.

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.18.87 and 20.4.2.15 describe AutoFit content widths
and wrapNone's exclusion from text wrapping. The native behavior clarifies that
unwrapped floating extents are excluded from AutoFit; no spec divergence is
claimed. Inline pictures and wrapped drawings keep their width contributions.
